title: build_lambdas.sh shipped stale calgen from uv cache
description:
calgen's version is pinned at 0.1.0 and never changes, so uv treated the locally-built wheel as cache-valid and reused it even after packages/calgen source changed. Lambda bundles and the CodeBuild wheel silently shipped pre-edit code.

Caught while working next_dctech_events-7lg: the deployed iCal aggregator contained zero references to HORIZON_DAYS after a clean build_lambdas.sh run and deploy, so the 180-day horizon had no effect in production despite the source being correct and passing local tests (the local venv uses an editable install, which reads source directly and therefore masked the problem).

Fixed by forcing a rebuild in all three places calgen is packaged:
  CALGEN_FRESH=(--refresh-package calgen --reinstall-package calgen)  # both uv pip install targets
  uv build --no-cache ...                                            # CodeBuild wheel

## Context
Worth remembering: an editable install in cdk_next/.venv means local pytest and local calgen builds always see current source, so this class of bug cannot be caught locally — only by inspecting the built artifact or the deployed function.
acceptance_criteria: After editing packages/calgen source, ./build_lambdas.sh produces bundles and a wheel containing the edit. Verified by grepping build/ical_aggregator/calgen, build/newsletter/calgen, and the built wheel.

title: db.py drops skip_phrases when reading GROUP items
description:
_group_item_to_dict in cdk_next/lambda_src/api/db.py copies a fixed allowlist of fields off the GROUP# item:

    for field in ['website', 'ical', 'fallback_url', 'categories',
                  'suppress_urls', 'suppress_guid', 'scan_for_metadata', 'url_override']:

skip_phrases is absent, so the field is silently discarded on every read even though put_group writes it and the migration carried it over from _groups/*.yaml (nvtc.yaml sets it). Anything reading groups through this helper — the site-generator export, the iCal aggregator, and the MCP list_groups tool — never sees it.

## Context
Introduced when backend/db.py was forked for this stack. One-line fix, but it blocks any skip_phrases support in calgen from taking effect.
acceptance_criteria: skip_phrases survives a get_group/get_all_groups round-trip and reaches _groups/*.yaml via export_dynamo_to_calgen.py.

title: Cap iCal fetch horizon at 180 days
description:
The vendored calgen has no upper bound on how far ahead it keeps iCal events, so dctech.events currently lists events out to 2029. The pre-cutover site capped them at 180 days.

In packages/calgen/src/calgen/calendars.py, fetch_ical_and_extract_events expands each VEVENT with an rrule individually over a 90-day window (recurring_end_dt) but applies no horizon at all to non-recurring events. Upstream replaced this with a single whole-calendar expansion bounded at 180 days:

    start_dt = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    end_dt = start_dt + timedelta(days=180)
    for event in recurring_ical_events.of(cal).between(start_dt, end_dt):

Measured against the live AFCEA feed: the current code yields 76 events through 2027-06, the 180-day form yields 39 through 2027-01.

## Context
Behaviour exists in the now-archived rosskarchner/calgen at origin/main (commit ce08c53 lineage), fetchable from the local checkout at ~/projects/calgen. Never ported when calgen was vendored, because the vendored copy came from a local working tree that predated it.
acceptance_criteria: Events beyond 180 days no longer appear on dctech.events. The iCal aggregator's prune step removes the now-out-of-horizon EVENT# items on its next run (expect roughly 96 removals). Site build succeeds and the homepage/month pages still render.

title: Port weekly cleanup of unconfirmed Cognito users
description:
The old dctech-events-api stack ran dctech-events-cleanup-unconfirmed-users on cron(0 2 ? * SUN *), deleting unconfirmed users from the shared pool us-east-1_8Ay4dTt8j. It last ran 2026-08-01 and was removed when that stack was deleted during decommissioning.

The pool is now adopted by this stack and still accumulates unconfirmed signups, so the hygiene job is still wanted. Source is in the old repo at cleanup_unconfirmed_users/handler.py; it needs cognito-idp:ListUsers and AdminDeleteUser on the pool.
acceptance_criteria: A scheduled Lambda in this stack removes unconfirmed users older than the previous threshold, with the same weekly cadence.

title: Normalize invisible Unicode in event titles
description:
Event titles arriving from iCal feeds can contain zero-width and other invisible Unicode characters. Left in place they break two things:

- skip_phrases matching, since a title with a zero-width space no longer matches the configured phrase
- duplicate detection, since are_events_duplicates in packages/calgen/src/calgen/pipeline.py compares titles exactly, and calculate_event_hash in event_utils.py folds the title into the guid — so the same event can churn guids or fail to dedupe

Upstream strips these characters in event_utils.py before hashing and in pipeline.py before comparison.

## Context
Behaviour exists in the now-archived rosskarchner/calgen at origin/main (commit 3c9246e, 'Fix invisible Unicode chars breaking skip_phrases filtering and duplicate detection'), fetchable from ~/projects/calgen. Note this changes guids for any affected event, so expect one-time churn: the aggregator will write new EVENT# items and prune the old ones. Upstream also ships tests/test_unicode_normalization.py worth porting alongside.
acceptance_criteria: Titles differing only by invisible characters produce the same guid and dedupe against each other; skip_phrases matching is unaffected by them.

title: Port skip_phrases group filtering into calgen
description:
Groups can declare skip_phrases to drop matching events from their feed. The vendored calgen ignores the field entirely, so those events publish. _groups/nvtc.yaml sets:

    skip_phrases:
      - COMMUNITY TUESDAYS AT REFRACTION

and roughly 15 such events are currently live on dctech.events; the pre-cutover site filtered them.

Upstream implements the match in packages/calgen/src/calgen/pipeline.py during event processing, case-insensitively against the event title.

## Context
Behaviour exists in the now-archived rosskarchner/calgen at origin/main (commit ce08c53), fetchable from ~/projects/calgen. Blocked by the db.py read bug — until that is fixed the field never reaches calgen even if the matching logic is ported.
acceptance_criteria: Events whose titles match a group's skip_phrases are absent from _data/all_events.json and the built site. The nvtc 'Community Tuesdays at Refraction' events stop appearing.
notes: Working as intended, with a correction to this ticket's premise. The nvtc feed publishes 2 'Community Tuesdays at Refraction' copies and skip_phrases now drops both. The 13 that remain on the site are source='recurring' — a curated RECURRING# definition expanded over 90 days — which group-level skip_phrases does not (and should not) touch. That is exactly why the phrase was configured: suppress the feed duplicates, keep the curated series. Live site now shows 13, matching the pre-cutover site's 13. The ticket's '~15 such events show' figure came from a grep that conflated occurrences.
